"'''Kiss from a Rose'''" is a song from British singer-songwriter [[Seal (musician)|Seal]]'s [[Seal (1994 album)|second eponymous album]] (1994). The song was first released as a single in July 1994 by [[ZTT Records]] and was included in the film ''[[The NeverEnding Story III]]'' that year.

The song was re-released a year later in 1995 as part of the [[Batman Forever (soundtrack)|''Batman Forever'' film soundtrack]], helping it top the charts in the United States and Australia. The song also reached the top 10 in several other countries, including Canada, France, Iceland and Norway. At the [[1996 Grammy Awards]], it won awards for [[Grammy Award for Record of the Year|Record of the Year]], [[Grammy Award for Song of the Year|Song of the Year]], and [[Grammy Award for Best Male Pop Vocal Performance|Best Male Pop Vocal Performance]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Past Winners Search|url=http://www.grammy.com/nominees/search?year=1995|work=Grammy.com|access-date=18 June 2013}}</ref> Two different music videos were produced to promote the single, directed by [[Matthew Rolston]] and [[Joel Schumacher]], respectively.

"Kiss from a Rose" is a song from British singer-songwriter Seal's second eponymous album (1994). The song was first released as a single in July 1994 by ZTT Records and was included in the film The NeverEnding Story III that year.

The song was re-released a year later in 1995 as part of the Batman Forever film soundtrack, helping it top the charts in the United States and Australia. The song also reached the top 10 in several other countries, including Canada, France, Iceland and Norway. At the 1996 Grammy Awards, it won awards for Record of the Year, Song of the Year, and Best Male Pop Vocal Performance. Two different music videos were produced to promote the single, directed by Matthew Rolston and Joel Schumacher, respectively.

sections.heading: Background
Critical reception
sections.wikitext:
Melinda Newman from ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' magazine wrote, "The swelling music of the sexy mid-tempo ballad 'Kiss from a Rose' hypnotizes as it enchants."<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Melinda|last=Newman|url=https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Billboard/90s/1994/BB-1994-05-28.pdf#page=11|title=The Beat: Seal Delivers On Fab Sophomore Set; Recording Added To School Curriculum|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=28 May 1994|page=11|access-date=16 May 2025}}</ref> Chuck Campbell from ''[[Knoxville News Sentinel]]'' felt that "fairy-tale-ish melodies and harmonies" uplift the song.<ref>Campbell, Chuck (17 June 1994). "McLachlan Explores Love At Its Darkest". ''[[Knoxville News Sentinel]]''.</ref> Ian Gittins from ''[[Melody Maker]]'' noted its "would-be butterfly sigh".<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Ian|last=Gittins|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/nothingelseon/53169588713/|title=Albums|magazine=[[Melody Maker]]|date=4 June 1994|page=34|access-date=7 September 2023}}</ref> Another ''Melody Maker'' editor, [[Andrew Mueller]], named it "a nondescript wine bar ballad".<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Andrew|last=Mueller|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/nothingelseon/53221611747/|title=Singles|magazine=[[Melody Maker]]|date=6 August 1994|page=31|access-date=1 October 2023|author-link=Andrew Mueller}}</ref> Pan-European magazine ''[[Music & Media]]'' commented, "Sealed with a kiss, here you get a [[ballad]] and a half! It's got the right pathos and the unavoidable violins. The thorn, needed to show the sincerity, comes from the razor sharp alto sax".<ref>{{cite magazine|first= |last= |title= New Releases: Singles |magazine= [[Music & Media]] |volume= 11 |issue= 33 |date= 13 August 1994 |page= 6 |accessdate= 14 March 2021 |url= https://worldradiohistory.com/UK/Music-and-Media/90s/1994/MM-1994-08-13.pdf}}</ref>{{unreliable source?|date=February 2026|reason=This song has no saxophone.}}

Alan Jones from ''[[Music Week]]'' wrote, "Seal's magnificent 'Kiss from a Rose' – now subtitled 'Love Theme from ''Batman Forever''{{'}} – is back a mere year after its first release when it reached number 19. A complex yet melodic song, it has remained a radio staple since it was first released, and is ready to explode".<ref>{{cite magazine|first= Alan |last= Jones |title= Talking Music |magazine= [[Music Week]] |date= 15 July 1995 |page= 29 |accessdate= 10 May 2021 |url= https://worldradiohistory.com/UK/Music-Week/1995/Music-Week-1995-07-15.pdf}}</ref> Leesa Daniels from ''[[Smash Hits]]'' gave it a top score of five out of five and named it Best New Single, saying, "A glorious ballad that will send shivers up and down your spine as soon as Seal opens his mouth. It's very atmospheric and moody, you can almost see the dry ice they'll use to death in the video. More importantly, it's one tune that you'll never, ever get bored of listening to."<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Leesa|last=Daniels|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/smashhits90s/34884065894/in/album-72157683731439410|title=Singles|magazine=[[Smash Hits]]|date=5 July 1995|page=54|access-date=9 February 2025}}</ref> Another ''Smash Hits'' editor, Emma Cochrane, remarked that it "shows what an incredible range his voice has".<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Emma|last=Cochrane|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/smashhits90s/34999451636/in/album-72157682568545460/|title=New Albums|magazine=[[Smash Hits]]|date=25 May 1994|page=48|access-date=6 October 2024}}</ref>
sections.text:
Melinda Newman from Billboard magazine wrote, "The swelling music of the sexy mid-tempo ballad 'Kiss from a Rose' hypnotizes as it enchants." Chuck Campbell from Knoxville News Sentinel felt that "fairy-tale-ish melodies and harmonies" uplift the song. Ian Gittins from Melody Maker noted its "would-be butterfly sigh". Another Melody Maker editor, Andrew Mueller, named it "a nondescript wine bar ballad". Pan-European magazine Music & Media commented, "Sealed with a kiss, here you get a ballad and a half! It's got the right pathos and the unavoidable violins. The thorn, needed to show the sincerity, comes from the razor sharp alto sax".{{unreliable source?|date=February 2026|reason=This song has no saxophone.}}

Alan Jones from Music Week wrote, "Seal's magnificent 'Kiss from a Rose' – now subtitled 'Love Theme from Batman Forever{{'}} – is back a mere year after its first release when it reached number 19. A complex yet melodic song, it has remained a radio staple since it was first released, and is ready to explode". Leesa Daniels from Smash Hits gave it a top score of five out of five and named it Best New Single, saying, "A glorious ballad that will send shivers up and down your spine as soon as Seal opens his mouth. It's very atmospheric and moody, you can almost see the dry ice they'll use to death in the video. More importantly, it's one tune that you'll never, ever get bored of listening to." Another Smash Hits editor, Emma Cochrane, remarked that it "shows what an incredible range his voice has".

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
Two versions of the music video for "Kiss from a Rose" were produced:
* The original version is set in a [[photographic studio]] and was co-directed by [[Matthew Rolston]] and William Levin. The 1966 film ''[[Blowup]]'' was heavily referenced in the video.
* The second version was directed by [[Joel Schumacher]] and has Seal performing the song beside the [[Bat-Signal]], interspersed with clips from the film ''[[Batman Forever]]''. This is the more well known video of the song. The director of photography was Neil Abramson.

sections.heading: Legacy
sections.wikitext: "Kiss from a Rose" was ranked number 90 on ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'''s "The 100 Greatest Summer Songs", saying, "Imagine [[Al Green]] in [[Camelot]]: Hitching a medieval melody to an [[Contemporary R&B|R&B]] [[Soul music|soul]], Seal delivered a stunner as haunted and timeless as '[[Sea of Love (Phil Phillips song)|Sea of Love]]'."<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.ew.com/ew/gallery/0,,20201383_20201385_20202309_10,00.html|title=The 100 Greatest Summer Songs: Nos. 100–76|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|date=2009|access-date=2 April 2025|archive-date=27 February 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090227041026/http://www.ew.com/ew/gallery/0,,20201383_20201385_20202309_10,00.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

sections.heading: Track listing
sections.wikitext:
Between all the formats of the single release, bonus tracks include the non-album tracks "[[The Wind Cries Mary]]" (a [[Jimi Hendrix]] cover) and "Blues in 'E'"; remixes of "Kiss from a Rose" by [[Adamski]] (who produced the original version of "[[Killer (Seal song)|Killer]]"); and remixes of album track "I'm Alive" by [[Steve Fitzmaurice]] and [[Sasha (DJ)|Sasha]] with [[BT (musician)|BT]].

* "Kiss from a Rose" {{small|(radio edit)}} – 3:38
* "Kiss from a Rose" {{small|(album version)}} – 4:47
